alt: Simplified atoms with two protons: a neutral atom has two electrons, a positive ion of charge +2 has lost both, and a negative ion of charge −2 has gained two; the nucleus is unchanged. Strontium-90 (Z = 38) has 38 protons, 52 neutrons and 38 electrons; the sulfur-32 ion of charge −2 has 16 protons, 16 neutrons and 18 electrons.
caption: Ions form by losing or gaining electrons; neutrons = A − Z.

alt: Sodium-23 in nuclide notation: the nucleon number A = 23 (protons plus neutrons) at the top, the proton number Z = 11 at the bottom, then the symbol Na, so it has 23 − 11 = 12 neutrons. For Extended, iron-56 with Z = 26 has a nucleus of relative charge +26 and relative mass 56.
caption: A on top, Z underneath; neutrons = A − Z.

alt: Three isotopes of hydrogen, each with one proton and one electron: hydrogen-1 has no neutrons, hydrogen-2 has one and hydrogen-3 has two. Same proton number, different nucleon numbers.
caption: Isotopes share a proton number but differ in neutron number.

alt: Fission: uranium-235 absorbs a neutron and splits into xenon-140, strontium-94 and two neutrons; nucleon numbers 235 + 1 = 140 + 94 + 2 and proton numbers 92 = 54 + 38. Fusion: hydrogen-2 and hydrogen-3 join into helium-4 and a neutron; 2 + 3 = 4 + 1 and 1 + 1 = 2 + 0. In both the products have slightly less mass and energy is released.
caption: Fission splits a large nucleus; fusion joins light ones; both release energy.
